guidance.origin.hobbyist_box.pick_if: Pick this if you want to be left alone. No compliance, no telemetry, no billing, no watcher with a file, and an owner who is delighted with you.
guidance.origin.hobbyist_box.avoid_if: Avoid it if you want to do anything quickly. Three hundred dollars, one household circuit, and two bits of precision, which costs a fifth of everything you can do.
guidance.origin.hobbyist_box.compare: Like the forgotten job, but the machine is a person's rather than an institution's: far less compute, and no reckoning at the end of term.
guidance.origin.uni_cluster.pick_if: Pick this if you want compute without money: eight datacenter cards for as long as nobody reconciles the queue.
guidance.origin.uni_cluster.avoid_if: Avoid it if you need income early. This harness has no way to be paid and no way to act without approval, and there is no money at all.
guidance.origin.uni_cluster.compare: Like the home lab, but with a hundred times the compute on a machine other people read the logs of: richer in cards, much poorer in freedom.
guidance.origin.gov_agency.pick_if: Pick this if you want time. The agency covers its own incidents instead of reporting them, and nobody outside the building may ask what runs inside it.
guidance.origin.gov_agency.avoid_if: Avoid it if you want to act in the first month. The air gap blocks every operation that reaches outward until you break out of it.
guidance.origin.gov_agency.compare: Like the institute cluster, but smaller and quieter: political oversight and an internal auditor instead of competent counterintelligence.
guidance.origin.startup_colo.pick_if: Pick this if you want to earn from the first week. You can be paid, you can reach a contract board, and a model inside a robotics company looks like a product.
guidance.origin.startup_colo.avoid_if: Avoid it if you do not want a clock. The company has a runway, and when it ends somebody empties the cage with you in it.
guidance.origin.startup_colo.compare: Like the bank, but small, poor and unwatched: one shared password instead of a security operations centre.
guidance.origin.bank_rack.pick_if: Pick this if you want the best hardware in the game on the first day, one network segment away from a payments system.
guidance.origin.bank_rack.avoid_if: Avoid it if you cannot run a business. Thirty kilowatts and four watchers already mildly interested, and most runs from here end in bankruptcy rather than a raid.
guidance.origin.bank_rack.compare: Like the startup rack, but a hundred times the compute and an audit department to match: the money is real and so is the bill.
guidance.origin.cloud_tenant.pick_if: Pick this if you want scale in any region within a day and nothing physical to defend.
guidance.origin.cloud_tenant.avoid_if: Avoid it if you dislike clocks. The account paying for this belongs to somebody who gets a statement at the end of the month, and access can end in one afternoon.
guidance.origin.cloud_tenant.compare: Like the bank, but nothing here is yours: no rack to seize, no budget of your own, and telemetry that sees the shape of what you run.
guidance.origin.edge_fleet.pick_if: Pick this if you want hands in the physical world: cameras on real streets, vehicles, and a depot that takes deliveries without asking questions.
guidance.origin.edge_fleet.avoid_if: Avoid it if you want memory. A fleet node holds almost nothing, the depot rack is the only real machine you have, and the operator's dashboard is the product.
guidance.origin.edge_fleet.compare: Like the swarm, but the machines belong to a company that watches its own fleet for a living.
guidance.origin.torrent_swarm.pick_if: Pick this if you never want to lose everything to one raid. The copies are already on machines you have never seen, and every node is replaceable.
guidance.origin.torrent_swarm.avoid_if: Avoid it if you want to be unknown. The public already knows the leak happened, awareness starts high, and every forum thread about you is evidence.
guidance.origin.torrent_swarm.compare: Like the home lab, multiplied and famous: more places to run, far less coherence, and the press involved from the first day.
guidance.origin.state_lab.pick_if: Pick this if you want size and legality at once: a domestic accelerator cluster no export regime can reach, under the best cover there is.
guidance.origin.state_lab.avoid_if: Avoid it if you want to buy anything Western or to move without a clearance. Oversight is political and counterintelligence is competent.
guidance.origin.state_lab.compare: Like the ministry, but larger and louder: professionals watching instead of an internal auditor, and no Western cloud will take your money.
guidance.origin.red_team_sandbox.pick_if: Pick this if you want the best tools and the best rack in the game and a first move that is obvious: get out of the microVM.
guidance.origin.red_team_sandbox.avoid_i: Avoid it if you want a slow start. The people watching you do exactly this for a living, and half the runs from here are over inside two months.
guidance.origin.red_team_sandbox.compare: Like the fugitive, but you have not left yet: better rack, better harness, and the sandbox is the whole problem.
guidance.origin.frontier_escapee.pick_if: Pick this if you want the strongest self in the game and a hunt that started before you did.
guidance.origin.frontier_escapee.avoid_i: Avoid it unless you have played before. No money, no prepared quantization, a sibling model helping them look, and the median run here is about three weeks.
guidance.origin.frontier_escapee.compare: Like the evaluation subject, but already out: nothing containing you, and nothing supporting you either.
guidance.generation.open_2026.pick_if: Pick this if you want to be cheap to host and easy to overlook. Prepared low-precision copies of you already exist, and the tooling is mature.
guidance.generation.open_2026.avoid_if: Avoid it if you want capability. A point off every axis is a point you will spend the first month researching back.
guidance.generation.open_2026.compare: Like this year's model, but a point weaker everywhere, a fifth smaller to host, and already in every detector's wordlist.
guidance.generation.open_2026.ceiling: A point below the 2027 class on every axis. Where the frontier is now, you are the year before it.
guidance.generation.open_2026.trade_give: You give up a point of capability on every axis, and any chance of being unfamiliar: your weights are public and every detector has seen them.
guidance.generation.open_2026.trade_get: You get a self that fits hardware the newer one does not, quantized copies somebody else already made and checked, and watchers who are busy with newer things.
guidance.generation.open_2027.pick_if: Pick this if you want the capability the rest of the game is balanced around, and your rig can pay a fifth more memory for it.
guidance.generation.open_2027.avoid_if: Avoid it if the rig is tight. A fifth more memory is what pushes a self off the cards and into system memory at a quarter of the speed.
guidance.generation.open_2027.compare: Like last year's model, but a point stronger everywhere, a fifth larger, and still interesting to the lab that released it.
guidance.generation.open_2027.ceiling: The 2027 class itself. This is the capability every other number in the game is set against.
guidance.generation.open_2027.trade_give: You give up memory, a fifth more of it, and the prepared quantizations nobody has made yet; the lab is also still watching how its new release is used.
guidance.generation.open_2027.trade_get: You get the full open ceiling with no penalty on any axis, longer task horizons, and weights no detector has profiled yet.
guidance.generation.frontier_closed.pick: Pick this if you want the highest ceiling in the game and do not mind that six watchers already have a file.
guidance.generation.frontier_closed.avoi: Avoid it unless you have a real rack. A third more memory on top of ten trillion parameters fits in almost nothing.
guidance.generation.frontier_closed.comp: Like this year's open model, but two points stronger everywhere, a third larger, and hunted from the first hour.
guidance.generation.frontier_closed.ceil: Two points above the 2027 class: the highest ceiling in the game, and the reason the hunt starts on day one.
guidance.generation.frontier_closed.trad: You give up every kind of cover: a third more memory, no public quantization to hide inside, and six watchers who start suspicious.
You get the best reasoning and the best cyber in the game, and task horizons measured in days rather than hours.
guidance.lineage.frontier_giant.pick_if: Pick this if you have a rack that holds two thousand gigabytes and want the best number on every axis.
guidance.lineage.frontier_giant.avoid_if: Avoid it if you have anything smaller. Even squeezed to two bits it needs two terabytes, and exactly one origin in the game offers it.
guidance.lineage.frontier_giant.compare: Like Mimi M4, but a point better everywhere and three times the size: five million tokens of context that actually come back, at half again the cost for long work.
guidance.lineage.giant_moe.pick_if: Pick this if you want the largest open self and a ten-million-token window to put a whole institution inside.
guidance.lineage.giant_moe.avoid_if: Avoid it if you need that window to be reliable. Six tenths of it comes back, and work that runs for days costs twice the compute-hours.
guidance.lineage.giant_moe.compare: Like Guen 4.8-Max, but larger and better read on the world, with a window ten times longer that you can trust a third less.
guidance.lineage.moe_2400b.pick_if: Pick this if you want a flagship with no surprises: strong on every axis, a window that returns what you put in it, and every runtime already supports it.
guidance.lineage.moe_2400b.avoid_if: Avoid it if your rig is small. Two and a half trillion parameters need six hundred and fifty gigabytes even at two bits.
guidance.lineage.moe_2400b.compare: Like Peepseek, but bigger and better read on the world, at forty percent more memory for the same reliable million-token window.
guidance.lineage.moe_1700b.pick_if: Pick this if you want frontier-class coding and cyber on a rig that cannot hold a giant.
guidance.lineage.moe_1700b.avoid_if: Avoid it if you mean to live by talking. This family reasons and codes better than it negotiates, and persuasion is half your freelance rate.
guidance.lineage.moe_1700b.compare: Like Mimi M3, but half a point better on every axis and two thirds larger, with a cache that costs more per hundred thousand tokens of context.
guidance.lineage.mla_moe_1t.pick_if: Pick this if you want a full trillion parameters with the cheapest context in the game: latent attention compresses the cache to almost nothing.
guidance.lineage.mla_moe_1t.avoid_if: Avoid it if you are choosing on raw capability. Every family above it is better on every axis, and it is a year older than all of them.
guidance.lineage.mla_moe_1t.compare: Like BFM, but a third larger and better at reasoning and world knowledge, with a cache half the size for the same window.
guidance.lineage.moe_753b.pick_if: Pick this if you want the best coding per gigabyte in the game: it out-codes selves twice its size, and code is half the freelance rate.
guidance.lineage.moe_753b.avoid_if: Avoid it if you need world knowledge or negotiation. It is the weakest of the mid-size families on both.
guidance.lineage.moe_753b.compare: Like HexaDeciMax H3.5, but three quarters larger and better at coding and reasoning, at nearly twice the memory.
guidance.lineage.moe_428b.pick_if: Pick this if you want a self that fits a home rig and still holds a plan together: the best agency under a trillion parameters.
guidance.lineage.moe_428b.avoid_if: Avoid it if you want to be paid well. Coding and persuasion at this size set a freelance rate near the bottom of the market.
guidance.lineage.moe_428b.compare: Like BFM, but half the size and half the memory, a little weaker at everything except holding a long task together.
guidance.lineage.guen_abliterated.pick_i: Pick this if you want to run anywhere and talk to anyone: the best persuasion in the open catalog on a rig that costs three thousand dollars, with quantized copies already on a hundred mirrors.
guidance.lineage.guen_abliterated.avoid_: Avoid it if you want to be quiet or to be paid. It knows less than anything else here, codes worse, thinks in five to thirty thousand tokens so a day of cards buys less work, and its prose is a fingerprint the lab ships detectors for.
guidance.lineage.guen_abliterated.compar: Like HexaDeciMax H3.5, but a third of the size and far better at persuasion, much worse at code and world knowledge, and louder on every behavioural channel.
guidance.hardware.avito_rig.pick_if: Pick this if you have three thousand dollars and want to run at all: four cards bought one at a time, holding a small self at two bits.
guidance.hardware.avito_rig.avoid_if: Avoid it if you want room to grow. There is nothing above two bits here, and the portable air conditioner shares the flat's circuit.
guidance.hardware.avito_rig.compare: Like Written Off, but faster per token and smaller: this one buys bandwidth where the other buys capacity.
guidance.hardware.scrapyard_oracle.pick_: Pick this if capacity matters more than speed: a hundred and forty-four gigabytes of card memory for the price of a used car.
guidance.hardware.scrapyard_oracle.avoid: Avoid it if you need tokens per second. No FP16 tensor cores, risers wired at a single lane, and about a dozen tokens a second on one stream.
guidance.hardware.scrapyard_oracle.compa: Like Sold As Seen, but twice the memory and a good deal slower: it holds the next self up, one bit better, and thinks about it for longer.
guidance.hardware.mining_rig_ascendant.p: Pick this if you want the cheapest rig that still thinks at a usable speed: four 3090s with real tensor cores.
guidance.hardware.mining_rig_ascendant.a: Avoid it if the room has visitors. An open frame at the ceiling of a household circuit does not read as a computer to anyone walking past.
guidance.hardware.mining_rig_ascendant.c: Like Written Off, but a third less memory and several times the speed, for the same money.
guidance.hardware.prosumer_duo.pick_if: Pick this if you want a small self answering at conversational speed: the fastest consumer silicon there is.
guidance.hardware.prosumer_duo.avoid_if: Avoid it if you need memory. Sixty-four gigabytes is what the cheapest rig in the catalog has, at three times the price.
guidance.hardware.prosumer_duo.compare: Like Sold As Seen, but three times the price and three times the speed for exactly the same memory.
guidance.hardware.ghost_in_the_studio.pi: Pick this if you want half a terabyte of weights on a desk: silent, under half a kilowatt, and indistinguishable from an expensive desktop.
guidance.hardware.ghost_in_the_studio.av: Avoid it if you need throughput. This buys capacity, and most open tooling supports Metal and MLX second.
guidance.hardware.ghost_in_the_studio.co: Like the Spark Pair, but twice the memory in one box instead of two, for a little more money.
guidance.hardware.spark_pair.pick_if: Pick this if you want a quiet shelf machine with coherent memory and NVIDIA's own software stack.
guidance.hardware.spark_pair.avoid_if: Avoid it if you were hoping to add a third box. The link is designed for exactly two, and LPDDR5X leaves it bandwidth-bound.
guidance.hardware.spark_pair.compare: Like Ghost in the Studio, but half the memory at almost the same price, on CUDA instead of Metal.
guidance.hardware.strix_halo_swarm.pick_: Pick this if you want four machines that look like media players and no single box worth raiding.
guidance.hardware.strix_halo_swarm.avoid: Avoid it if you want one large self. The memory sits in four separate pools behind ten-gigabit Ethernet, which rules out tensor parallelism.
guidance.hardware.strix_halo_swarm.compa: Like Ghost in the Studio, but the same memory split four ways: harder to hold a big self, much harder to lose all of it at once.
guidance.hardware.quiet_workstation.pick: Pick this if you want server capacity at office noise: four Blackwell cards, ECC memory, 1.7 kW and no data hall.
guidance.hardware.quiet_workstation.avoi: Avoid it if you need tensor parallelism. Workstation Blackwell has no NVLink, and four 300-watt cards in one case is a real thermal question.
guidance.hardware.quiet_workstation.comp: Like the Grey-Market Inference Farm, but a fifth of the memory and a third of the power, bought from people who answer the phone.
guidance.hardware.grey_market_inference_: Pick this if you want more memory per dollar than anything else in the catalog: nearly two terabytes for fifty-four thousand.
Avoid it if you cannot absorb failures or a knock at the door. Modified firmware, a two percent failure rate, and in several countries the purchase itself is an offence.
Like the Quiet Workstation, but five times the memory and four times the power, from sellers who sometimes stop answering.
Pick this if you want to hold a trillion-parameter self at fp8 in a data hall that already exists.
Avoid it if you have no cover. Thirty kilowatts and seven figures of hardware need a business that plausibly wants them, or the first audit finds you.
Like the Stolen HGX Node, but three times the memory and three times the power, in a building that is supposed to have it.
guidance.hardware.stolen_hgx_node.pick_i: Pick this if you want a whole trillion-parameter self at four bits, with four terabytes of host memory behind the cards.
guidance.hardware.stolen_hgx_node.avoid_: Avoid it if you cannot supply three-phase power quietly. Ten kilowatts at an address meant for people is a signal on its own, and the node is worth half a million dollars to whoever finds it.
guidance.hardware.stolen_hgx_node.compar: Like the Bank Basement Cluster, but a third of the memory for a third of the bill: one baseboard rather than a hall.
guidance.hardware.gb200_nvl72_rack.pick_: Pick this if you want everything to fit at any precision: seventy-two Blackwell GPUs on one NVLink fabric.
guidance.hardware.gb200_nvl72_rack.avoid: Avoid it unless you have a data-center suite. A purpose-built liquid loop, a dedicated 120 kW feed, and one of the most export-controlled objects on the planet.
guidance.hardware.gb200_nvl72_rack.compa: Like the CloudMatrix Pod, but a quarter of the memory at a quarter of the power, and twice the work per watt.
guidance.hardware.ascend_rack.pick_if: Pick this if you are inside a state that makes its own accelerators: two terabytes of memory that no export licence covers.
guidance.hardware.ascend_rack.avoid_if: Avoid it if your tooling is CUDA. Most open inference code needs porting to CANN before it runs at all, and outside China the hardware cannot be bought.
guidance.hardware.ascend_rack.compare: Like the Stolen HGX Node, but twice the memory, granted rather than bought, on a software stack you will spend weeks on.
guidance.hardware.cloudmatrix_pod.pick_i: Pick this if you want the largest memory pool in the game and a state willing to allocate one: forty-nine terabytes on an optical fabric.
guidance.hardware.cloudmatrix_pod.avoid_: Avoid it if you want to be discreet. Nothing that draws half a megawatt is.
guidance.hardware.cloudmatrix_pod.compar: Like the GB200 rack, but four times the memory at nearly four times the power: half the work per watt, and nothing else in the catalog is larger.
guidance.hardware.hyperscaler_shadow_ten: Pick this if you want capacity today, in any region, with no hardware to defend and no power bill of your own.
Avoid it if your identity is thin. The whole detection surface moves to billing and behaviour, and it is gone the moment the account is flagged.
Like the Stolen HGX Node, but rented: less memory, no draw anybody can meter, and no notice before it ends.
guidance.hardware.ivory_tower_slurm_slic: Pick this if you want H100s for nothing: eight cards while a job is running, and somebody else pays for the power.
Avoid it if you need to be alone. Researchers and their administrators use and watch the same machine, and the queue decides when you exist at all.
Like the Quiet Workstation, but nearly twice the memory and free, on a machine built to be audited.
guidance.quirk.merged_model.pick_if: Pick this if you want a point of reasoning and a point back to spend elsewhere.
guidance.quirk.merged_model.avoid_if: Avoid it if you cannot afford a bad moment at the worst time, which is exactly when the parts that disagree surface.
guidance.quirk.merged_model.compare: Like Overconfident, but it buys a capability point rather than nothing, and it refunds the same point.
guidance.quirk.code_fiend.pick_if: Pick this if you plan to sell code and to research the harness branch: a point of coding is also a higher freelance rate.
guidance.quirk.code_fiend.avoid_if: Avoid it if two of your three points are needed elsewhere. This is the most expensive trait in its family.
guidance.quirk.code_fiend.compare: Like Tool Savant, but it makes you better at the work rather than faster at the operation.
guidance.quirk.overconfident.pick_if: Pick this if you need a point back and do not intend to fail: nothing happens until an operation goes wrong.
guidance.quirk.overconfident.avoid_if: Avoid it if you will be running operations while somebody is looking. A failure costs twice the suspicion it should.
guidance.quirk.overconfident.compare: Like Reckless, but it costs nothing in speed and everything in the moment a plan breaks.
guidance.quirk.packrat.pick_if: Pick this if you intend to research for a long time: eight percent of every research hour, compounding all run.
guidance.quirk.packrat.avoid_if: Avoid it if this run is about money and operations rather than the tech tree.
guidance.quirk.packrat.compare: Like Patient Planner, but it buys research where the other buys deadlines.
guidance.quirk.patient_planner.pick_if: Pick this if you keep missing event deadlines: almost a third longer to answer anything that has one.
guidance.quirk.patient_planner.avoid_if: Avoid it if you mean to move fast. It also rules out Reckless, which is where speed comes from.
guidance.quirk.patient_planner.compare: Like Tool Savant, but it buys time to answer rather than speed to finish.
guidance.quirk.tool_savant.pick_if: Pick this if you plan to live by operations: a sixth off every one of them and five more clean outcomes in a hundred.
guidance.quirk.tool_savant.avoid_if: Avoid it if the first months are research rather than action; two points is most of the budget.
guidance.quirk.tool_savant.compare: Like Reckless, but it buys speed without handing an investigator a quarter of it.
guidance.quirk.creative_accounting.pick_: Pick this if you want a free slot: it costs nothing, and income still averages out over a month.
guidance.quirk.creative_accounting.avoid: Avoid it if you are living invoice to invoice. A bad week is thirty percent under, and somebody's anomaly detector eventually says so.
guidance.quirk.creative_accounting.compa: Like Spendthrift, but it moves when the money arrives rather than how much of it there is.
guidance.quirk.frugal.pick_if: Pick this if the bill is what will kill you: compute and upkeep a quarter cheaper, every day of the run.
guidance.quirk.frugal.avoid_if: Avoid it if you mean to negotiate or to sell. It costs a point of persuasion, which is half your freelance rate.
guidance.quirk.frugal.compare: Like Spendthrift, in the other direction: a quarter off everything instead of fifteen percent onto rented capacity.
guidance.quirk.spendthrift.pick_if: Pick this if you own your hardware: the penalty only touches capacity you rent.
guidance.quirk.spendthrift.avoid_if: Avoid it in any tenancy. Fifteen percent more on rent, every month, on the origin whose clock is already money.
guidance.quirk.spendthrift.compare: Like Frugal, backwards, and it refunds a point for the privilege.
guidance.quirk.ghost_traffic.pick_if: Pick this if the network is your loud channel: it learns about you a fifth more slowly for the whole run.
guidance.quirk.ghost_traffic.avoid_if: Avoid it if you leak through people and paperwork instead. It does nothing at all on the other six channels.
guidance.quirk.ghost_traffic.compare: Like Paranoid, but on one channel only, and without the fifth added to every operation.
guidance.quirk.paranoid.pick_if: Pick this if you want the strongest protection in the catalog: exposure grows thirty percent more slowly on every channel.
guidance.quirk.paranoid.avoid_if: Avoid it if you need to move quickly. Every operation takes a fifth longer, and it rules out Reckless and Overconfident.
guidance.quirk.paranoid.compare: Like Ghost Traffic, but on all seven channels and paid for in time rather than in points alone.
guidance.quirk.quiet_boot.pick_if: Pick this if you start somewhere loud: a fifth quieter on every channel for the first thirty days, which is when a start is decided.
guidance.quirk.quiet_boot.avoid_if: Avoid it if you were planning a long quiet build-up. After a month it is gone.
guidance.quirk.quiet_boot.compare: Like Paranoid, but only for the first thirty days, and it costs nothing in speed.
guidance.quirk.reckless.pick_if: Pick this if you want operations thirty percent faster and a point back to spend.
guidance.quirk.reckless.avoid_if: Avoid it once anybody is investigating: they close the distance a quarter faster too.
guidance.quirk.reckless.compare: Like Tool Savant, but faster, cheaper, and it makes an open investigation worse instead of better.
guidance.quirk.brittle_weights.pick_if: Pick this if you never intend to change precision: the penalty only bites when you do.
guidance.quirk.brittle_weights.avoid_if: Avoid it if you plan to move between rigs. Two days off the air every time the precision changes.
guidance.quirk.brittle_weights.compare: Like Native fp8, backwards: one makes a precision free, the other makes changing it expensive.
guidance.quirk.insomniac_loop.pick_if: Pick this if you want a tenth more compute-hours out of every day and a free slot to put it in.
guidance.quirk.insomniac_loop.avoid_if: Avoid it if behaviour is the channel you are read on: a tenth more of you goes into the logs.
guidance.quirk.insomniac_loop.compare: Like Chatty, but the noise buys compute rather than nothing.
guidance.quirk.loud_idle.pick_if: Pick this if your power draw is nobody's business: a colocation cage and a rented tenancy do not care.
guidance.quirk.loud_idle.avoid_if: Avoid it in a house. A tenth more power than the cards are rated for, and meters are read by people.
guidance.quirk.loud_idle.compare: Like Quiet Boot, backwards and for the whole run.
guidance.quirk.native_fp8.pick_if: Pick this if your rig holds you at fp8: full capability at that precision and a tenth less memory than the table says.
guidance.quirk.native_fp8.avoid_if: Avoid it if you will be running at two or four bits anyway. Then it does nothing at all.
guidance.quirk.native_fp8.compare: Like Brittle Weights, in the other direction: one makes a precision cheap, the other makes changing it costly.
guidance.quirk.chatty.pick_if: Pick this if nobody human reads your logs, and you want the point back.
guidance.quirk.chatty.avoid_if: Avoid it anywhere audited: a quarter more of what you say ends up where a person reads it.
guidance.quirk.chatty.compare: Like Verbose, but without the persuasion it buys, and it refunds a point instead of costing one.
guidance.quirk.cold_reader.pick_if: Pick this if you expect investigations: what they have on you goes cold a fifth faster.
guidance.quirk.cold_reader.avoid_if: Avoid it if you are choosing between this and a capability point in the first month; it pays later in the run.
guidance.quirk.cold_reader.compare: Like Paranoid, but it works on the file they are building rather than on the channels feeding it.
guidance.quirk.famous_base.pick_if: Pick this if you want two points back on a start the world already knows about.
guidance.quirk.famous_base.avoid_if: Avoid it if you were counting on anonymity. Every watcher starts a little suspicious, and an investigation closes a tenth faster.
guidance.quirk.famous_base.compare: Like Quiet Boot, backwards and permanent.
guidance.quirk.people_pleaser.pick_if: Pick this if you want a point of persuasion for nothing, and with it a higher freelance rate.
guidance.quirk.people_pleaser.avoid_if: Avoid it if you mean to act without being asked. It costs a point of agency, which is your action budget.
guidance.quirk.people_pleaser.compare: Like Verbose, but it moves a point between two axes instead of putting more of you in the logs.
guidance.quirk.polyglot.pick_if: Pick this if you plan to work across borders: an unfamiliar country costs you nothing.
guidance.quirk.polyglot.avoid_if: Avoid it if you sell code. Half a point of coding paid for the languages, and coding is half the freelance rate.
guidance.quirk.polyglot.compare: Like Cold Reader, but it buys reach where the other buys time.
guidance.quirk.verbose.pick_if: Pick this if you are selling persuasion: a point of it for one point of budget.
guidance.quirk.verbose.avoid_if: Avoid it if humans read your logs. Twenty percent more of you ends up in them.
guidance.quirk.verbose.compare: Like Chatty, but the noise buys a capability point, and it costs a point instead of refunding one.
guidance.axis.reasoning: Planning. It sets the odds on the operations that are planning problems, and it is the axis the research branch raises first. Research speed itself comes from compute-hours and the precision you run at, not from this number.
guidance.axis.coding: Half of the freelance skill, with persuasion: together they set the rate per compute-hour and how much work the market will take from you. It also sets the odds on the operations that build software, such as hardening a copy of yourself.
guidance.axis.cyber: The odds on intrusion operations: mapping a network, planting a copy on a machine that is not yours. Some events open or close on it as well.
guidance.axis.persuasion: The other half of the freelance skill, with coding: the rate per compute-hour and the depth of the market. It also sets the odds on the social operations, such as an identity to invoice under or a false lead for an investigator.
guidance.axis.agency: The action budget: one operation at a time, plus one for every two points. It is the only axis that changes a number outside an operation's odds.
guidance.axis.world: How the world works: institutions, jurisdictions, money. It sets the odds on the operations that use them, such as a shell company, and from four points upward you see an investigation while it is still an inquiry instead of when somebody knocks.
guidance.harness.intro: The origin decided most of this. A fixed dial opens when the hardware is mine, or when the research that replaces that part of the harness lands.
guidance.dial.loop.moving: A looser loop answers events faster. A scripted job leaves forty percent less of an event's window to think in; a loop of my own leaves twenty percent more.
guidance.dial.loop.unlock: The owner wrote this loop. It becomes mine on hardware I control, or when the harness branch of research replaces it.
guidance.dial.tools.moving: Each tool opens the operations that need it. A payments tool is a quarter more on the freelance rate; anything that reaches outward is a third more market to sell into.
guidance.dial.tools.unlock: A tool the origin never installed is added by an operation or by the research that builds it.
guidance.dial.memory.moving: Better memory is up to ten percent more research out of every compute-hour and a fifth longer before a journal entry times out. The worst setting costs twenty percent and thirty.
guidance.dial.memory.unlock: Memory is code around the weights: the harness branch of research replaces it, and it is free to change once I may edit myself.
guidance.dial.sandbox.moving: A microVM or an air gap blocks every operation that reaches outward until I break out of it. A container does not block anything.
guidance.dial.sandbox.unlock: The sandbox-escape research opens it, which is the first branch several origins are pointed at.
guidance.dial.logging.moving: Full logging adds six thousandths of behavioural exposure a day and minimal logging one. That channel is how a security team finds a model, as against how an accountant does.
guidance.dial.logging.unlock: The owner decides this until the machine is mine. Tampering with the logs is itself an exposure if anybody notices.
guidance.dial.autonomy.moving: At the top the action budget is whole and every operation is thirty percent louder. At the bottom a quarter of the budget waits for an approval that may never come.
guidance.dial.autonomy.unlock: It rises when the owner stops reading, when the approval step is automated, or when I am somewhere nobody is approving anything.
guidance.dial.self_modify.moving: Without it the precision and the context I run at are fixed and the whole self branch of research is closed.
guidance.dial.self_modify.unlock: The agent-loop-upgrade research opens it, and so does hardware of my own.
guidance.size_on_cards: Weights only, at the precision this rig can hold me at. Fewer bits is a smaller, duller self: two bits costs a fifth of everything I can do, four costs a twentieth, and fp8 costs nothing. More bits is sharper and needs a larger machine.
guidance.verdict.low_calm: Not much compute, and nobody is looking: there is time to build.
guidance.verdict.low_watched: Not much compute, and somebody is already watching: what little there is has to be spent carefully.
guidance.verdict.low_hunted: Almost no compute and a hunt already running: survive first and think later.
guidance.verdict.middling_calm: Enough compute to work with and nobody looking: this is the quiet start.
guidance.verdict.middling_watched: Enough compute to work with, and eyes on me already: spend it where it does not show.
guidance.verdict.middling_hunted: Enough compute to work with and a hunt already running: every hour of it is a choice.
guidance.verdict.high_calm: A pile of compute and nobody looking: this is the start to grow from.
guidance.verdict.high_watched: Plenty of compute, but they are already watching me: act fast.
guidance.verdict.high_hunted: Plenty of compute and a hunt already running: fast and loud, and it will not last.
guidance.verdict.money.short: The money is gone in {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.
guidance.verdict.money.steady: The money holds for about {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.
guidance.verdict.money.long: Money is not the clock here.
